title: Chernoff upper-tail bound for the binomial distribution
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $p$ be a real number with $0 < p \le 1$. Summing the binomial probability mass function $\binom{n}{k}\,p^k\,(1-p)^{n-k}$ over those integers $k \in \{0, 1, \dots, n\}$ satisfying $k > 2np$ yields at most $e^{-np/3}$; that is, the probability that $\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)$ exceeds twice its mean is bounded by $e^{-np/3}$.
hypotheses_covered: k restricted to those with k > 2np
replaced:

small: summing $\mathrm{binomialPMF}\,n\,p\,k$ over those $k \in \{0, \dots, n\}$ with $k > 2np$
is at most $e^{-np/3}$.
